message.content:
Sure! To start a Docker container on Windows, you’ll need to know the name or ID of the container you want to start. Once you have that, you can run:

```powershell
docker start <container_name_or_id>
```

If you’re looking to start the Docker Desktop service itself (so you can then run Docker commands), you can use:

```powershell
net start com.docker.service
```

Let me know which one you’d like to do, or provide the container name/ID so I can help you start it!
